learning_outcomes.text: You know the basic terminology of databases.

You are able to interpret an ERD structure and design it yourself based on functional requirements. You can convert this diagram into a concrete database. You understand how different tables are linked to each other and you can link them correctly yourself via foreign keys and intermediate tables.
Based on a business question, you write SQL statements that retrieve and display all data relevant to formulate an answer.
You write SQL statements for data manipulation: insert, update, delete.
You know the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases and write basic NoSQL statements.
You learn to work with DML (data manipulation language) - DDL (data definition language) - DCL (data control language).
You study the optimization of SQL queries.
You obtain a certificate for a cloud server.

syllabus_topics: Data Manipulation Language: basic and advanced regarding querying and editing data in a database
Select with group by, having, subquery, innerjoin, left- and right outerjoin, built-in functions, set operators
Data Definition Language: tables, views, referential integrity
Setting up ERD structure and converting to relational tables / Normalization
Data Control Language: user roles, grant, revoke
assessment_rules: The total grade is out of 20 points. The mid-term evaluation (lab) accounts for 5 points, the written theory exam for 7.5 points, and the written computer-based lab exam for 7.5 points. If absent during mid-term evaluations, exam rules apply. For resits, a successful partial result for theory (YT6215) or lab (YT6216) can be transferred within the academic year. If the total score is passing, even if one component is failing, no resit is required for that component. If the total score is failing, only the failing component needs to be re-taken, and the points from the successful component are retained.
